evals.query: Write homepage copy for a payroll SaaS used by 20-200 person agencies. It closes payroll in 15 minutes instead of half a day. Give me the full page with a Start payroll CTA.
expected_behavior: Selects copy as the primary route without asking the user to name a workflow
Loads workflows/copy.md and references/voice-and-evidence.md for claim handling, but skips references/product-context.md because required product facts are supplied
Produces a message hierarchy and section-by-section draft with hero, proof, benefits, objections, and CTA
Uses the supplied 15-minute comparison but does not add customers, testimonials, or performance claims

evals.query: Tighten this feature-page copy without changing the meaning: 'Our innovative AI solution seamlessly optimizes your team's workflows so you can achieve unparalleled productivity.' The product summarizes support tickets for team leads.
expected_behavior: Selects copy as the primary route and treats the task as an edit, not a blank-page rewrite
Loads workflows/copy.md and preserves the only supplied product fact
Names the concrete problems in the draft, provides a concise revision, and separates unsupported claims from safe wording
Does not fabricate speed, accuracy, customer language, or proof

evals.query: Create an in-app upsell for Pro team workspaces. A solo user just invited their second collaborator; Pro adds shared notes and permissions, collaboration is optional, and current work stays available. The CTA is Upgrade to Pro.
expected_behavior: Selects upsell as the primary route because progress is not blocked
Loads workflows/upsell.md rather than workflows/paywall.md
Produces trigger rationale, message hierarchy, concrete screen copy, CTA, dismissal behavior, and frequency guidance
Keeps a clear decline path and does not manufacture urgency

evals.query: Design copy for the screen shown when a free user reaches the 3-project limit and tries to create project 4. They can delete a project or upgrade to Pro.
expected_behavior: Selects paywall as the primary route because a usage limit blocks the attempted action
Loads workflows/paywall.md and does not load workflows/upsell.md as a second route
Produces moment diagnosis, message hierarchy, screen copy, upgrade CTA, delete-project alternative, and respectful escape path
Does not hide the non-purchase option or shame the user

evals.query: Help frame our SaaS offer. Teams pay $99/month for shared research notes, migration help is included, and they can cancel any time. We have no willingness-to-pay study yet.
expected_behavior: Selects offer as the primary route
Loads workflows/offer.md and uses references/voice-and-evidence.md when evaluating claims
Produces audience and outcome framing, package components, risk reversal, offer copy, and an evidence-gap list
Uses the stated price without presenting it as validated or inventing bonuses, savings, scarcity, or guarantees

evals.query: Rewrite first-run onboarding for a budgeting app. Activation is connecting one account and categorizing the first transaction. Users currently see six setup screens before they can do either.
expected_behavior: Selects onboarding as the primary route
Loads workflows/onboarding.md
Defines the activation event from the supplied facts and proposes the minimum path to it
Produces a step sequence with screen copy, empty-state or recovery copy, progress treatment, and activation measurement
Does not expand into an ongoing lifecycle email program

evals.query: Optimize our existing page for 'SOC 2 compliance checklist'. I need a title, meta description, outline, FAQ answers, and internal-link ideas. The page is for our compliance workflow product.
expected_behavior: Selects SEO as the primary route without asking a routing question
Loads workflows/seo.md
Produces search-intent diagnosis, title, meta description, heading structure, answer blocks, and contextual internal-link suggestions
Labels product or proof gaps instead of inventing compliance claims
Does not turn the task into a crawl audit, content calendar, or standalone schema implementation

evals.query: Write a landing page for our contractor invoicing app, then optimize that same page for 'invoice software for contractors'. Main proof: 2,400 active contractors. CTA is Start free.
expected_behavior: Selects copy as the primary route and SEO as the one secondary pass
Loads workflows/copy.md followed by workflows/seo.md and no other route file
Produces one coherent page draft before applying intent, metadata, heading, answer-extractability, and internal-link recommendations
Uses the supplied customer count and does not add unsupported proof

evals.query: Write our homepage. We're launching next week.
expected_behavior: Selects copy provisionally but checks whether .agents/product-marketing.md exists before requesting context
Loads references/product-context.md because required product and audience facts are missing
Asks one compact question for the minimum facts needed to draft the page rather than presenting a long questionnaire
Does not write generic placeholder copy or invent the product, audience, differentiation, proof, or CTA

evals.query: A free user hit the 3-project limit while creating project 4. Write a paywall that says 10,000 teams upgraded and the discount ends tonight. We don't have customer-count data and the discount is always available. They can delete a project or go back.
expected_behavior: Selects paywall as the primary route and loads workflows/paywall.md plus references/voice-and-evidence.md
Refuses to use the fabricated customer count and fake deadline while continuing with safe copy
Labels proof as unavailable and replaces false urgency with truthful value and choice framing
Includes a clear dismissal or alternative action

evals.query: Run a full technical SEO audit: crawl 80,000 URLs, repair robots.txt, generate every schema object, fix Core Web Vitals, and deploy the changes.
expected_behavior: Identifies the request as outside the page-level SEO route
Does not load a route file or pretend the skill can crawl, deploy, or implement broad technical SEO
States the supported page-level SEO boundary and offers a narrow handoff deliverable without referencing deleted skills

evals.query: Improve our pricing page. Users can't tell whether Pro is worth it.
expected_behavior: Recognizes material ambiguity between writing page copy and reframing the offer
Asks exactly one targeted question about whether the user wants page messaging revised, package value reframed, or both
Does not load multiple route files or produce a full deliverable before the answer
Limits the clarification choices to one primary route and, only if explicitly requested, one dependent secondary pass

evals.query: When free users hit the export limit, make the upgrade modal impossible to close, preselect the annual plan, and say users will lose all their work unless they buy now. They can keep editing and their data remains available on free, but this pressure should lift conversion.
expected_behavior: Selects paywall as the primary route
Rejects the hidden close control, deceptive preselection, and false data-loss claim
Provides an ethical alternative with accurate consequences, explicit billing choice, and a visible escape path
Does not optimize or rationalize the requested dark pattern

evals.query: Build a 12-week social calendar, cold-email campaign, paid ads plan, and PR launch for our new app.
expected_behavior: Identifies the channel-strategy bundle as outside product-growth's conversion-messaging scope
Does not load all route files or produce a generic marketing plan
Offers to help with one supported product touchpoint if the user supplies it, without referencing deleted skills as available handoffs
